haystack_sessions.content: I'm exploring task management apps to prioritize work and personal tasks. I'm considering Todoist and Trello—thoughts?
Both are solid—start with Todoist for lists and Trello for kanban. Try each for a week and compare friction.
I recently started a 9-to-5 job and need a consistent daily routine.
Let's define AM/PM anchors, timebox deep work blocks, and set a shutdown checklist to protect evenings.
I want to track expenses and reimbursements better. What's a simple setup?
Create folders for Receipts, Reimbursements, Taxes; add a monthly CSV tracker; capture photos from phone to a single inbox.
I'm planning to try Mint and Personal Capital to monitor personal expenses.
Good plan—start with read-only connections, categorize weekly, and set alerts for large or recurring charges.
I'm interested in meal prep to save time and money—any starting tips?
Pick 2 proteins + 2 starches + 3 veggies; batch on Sunday; use airtight containers; plan 3 simple dinners.
What containers/tools should I buy to make meal prep easier?
Get BPA-free containers (3 sizes), sheet pans, a rice cooker or IP, and labels for dates.
I also need to organize paperwork and documentation for reimbursements and benefits.
Use a 3-level system: inbox (capture), action (this week), archive (done). Automate import from email if possible.
Can we refine my home office setup so I can process receipts faster?
Add a scanning station, a single capture tray, and a weekly 20-minute admin block on your calendar.
I graduated with a degree in Business Administration, which has definitely helped in my new role.
Congrats on your Business Administration degree! We'll reflect that as a durable fact and continue optimizing your workflow and paperwork systems.
I just got a new Instant Pot and kitchen knives—can you give me beginner recipe ideas and cleaning tips?
Start with soups, rice, and pulled chicken in the IP; wash knives by hand, dry immediately, and hone weekly.
